assets.name: gentle hump
assets.geometry: solid under a cosine profile z(x) = crest/2 * (1 - cos(2*pi*x/length)), constant across the width; max slope = pi*crest/length = 5.9 deg
assets.collider: triangle mesh (static); not a convex hull: the concave ends would become a 4.3° straight ramp, up to 4.6 mm off (see assets/E1-gentle-hump/NOTES.md)
assets.reference_limits: FLUX image is illustrative; the cosine profile and sizes here are the spec

assets.name: low steps
assets.geometry: two stacked plywood sheets: bottom 1.2 x 0.6 x 0.010, top 0.8 x 0.6 x 0.010 centred on it (top surface at 0.020)

material.look: light birch plywood, visible ply edges

assets.collider: one box collider per sheet, so each tread is its own contact surface (as NVIDIA's ramp+steps asset)
assets.reference_limits: FLUX draws the top sheet off-centre and thicker than 1 cm; spec wins

assets.name: wet floor
assets.geometry: thin flat tile, flush look; 2 mm so it has a collider without being a step

material.look: glossy light-grey tile with shallow clear water puddles and a thin reflective film

assets.collider: one box collider with its own physics material (static and dynamic friction 0.3); verify how Newton combines foot and ground friction (max would cancel the low friction), see assets/E3-wet-floor/NOTES.md
assets.reference_limits: water is visual only; physics is low friction, no liquid

assets.name: box
assets.geometry: closed plywood box with one hand-hole cut-out on a side face

assets.name: floor and lane markings
assets.geometry: plane 6 x 1.2 m at z = 0; start and finish lines as 5 cm white tape painted into the texture at x 0.40 and 5.60 m (no geometry)
